releases.title: Your company, in the field
releases.summary: Recognizable miniatures, purpose-built architecture and a clearer view of the battle.
changes: The Builder carries his shoulder mallet beneath a broad straw hat; the Warrior bears the company shield; the Archer brings her copper hair and open bow to the battlefield. Their existing roles and combat rules stay the same.
Resource Camps have open supply shelters, Archery Ranges have practice targets, and Stables have timber bays. Each has matching teal and clay team materials.
Opening guidance steps aside while you manage workers, troops or settings, then returns with the current instruction. Placement guidance remains available.
Raid alerts remain reachable beside Economy and Army. Tap an alert to close management and view the threatened location while keeping your selected units.

releases.title: Room to learn. Room to play.
releases.summary: A full-screen battlefield, a gentler Easy opponent and architecture made for the company.
changes: Menu backgrounds and battlefields fill the phone screen. Controls stay clear of camera cutouts and the home indicator, including when you rotate the phone.
Easy sends smaller squads, gives you longer to establish your village and regroups after losing a fighter. Medium and Hard retain their pressure.
The Town Center, House and Barracks have original silhouettes, mineral roofs, timber details and pale stone. Enemy roofs and banners use clay colours while their materials stay natural.
Browser controls share the custom command plates. Notices use clearer type and quieter colours; the problem-report form respects the phone safe area.

releases.title: A company worth commanding
releases.summary: An original cast, bespoke controls and three battlefields with room for different tactics.
changes: Meet the Builder, Warrior and Archer in a new character-led menu. Custom command plates, equipment-inspired icons and quieter battlefield markers give the game a consistent identity.
Choose Open Plains, River Crossings or Woodland Flanks in Settings → Map. Save a seed to revisit a battlefield.
River maps have three broad crossings. Woodland maps offer attack lanes around deep forests. Both keep opening resources close and expansions reachable.
Online rivals receive the same map and seed. Updated players can meet on all three styles; matches with older clients retain Open Plains.
Melee fighters make room for allies while attacking, reducing stacks of units on a shared target.
The AI can rebalance its workers when another worker is unable to find a job, keeping paid military production moving.

releases.title: Find a rival. Build your kingdom.
releases.summary: Online 1v1, quicker openings and simpler touch controls.
changes: Choose Online 1v1 to search for another player. Matches run on a shared authoritative server; search can be cancelled and disconnects produce a clear result.
Tap ground to move without stopping for enemies. Hold ground to attack-move. Drag to pan, pinch to zoom, and use the area-selection icon before dragging around an army.
Build choices, worker management, training and settings fit compact pages without scrolling. Short, distinct markers show move, gather, attack and rally orders.
Farms provide food indefinitely. One Resource Camp accepts food, wood and gold; workers choose reachable drop-offs and preserve carried resources when reassigned.
Larger opening supplies, faster paid training and better delivery rates bring armies forward. Standard Sacred victory now requires three minutes of uninterrupted control.
Units keep movement intent under fire, defend nearby allies and limit autonomous pursuit. Production exits avoid isolated pockets beside buildings.

releases.title: A better fit for your phone
releases.summary: Cleaner shapes, less stacked interface and comfortable controls on smaller screens.
changes: Primary commands now use matching square buttons; extra orders open beside the management controls to leave more of the battlefield visible.
Build categories have compact tabs and consistently sized cards. Army fits its contents, while Economy adapts its worker controls to narrower screens.
Worker job counts live in Economy, removing a duplicate strip above the command dock. Names, prices, shortages and finite Farm food remain available where you make decisions.
Smaller screens automatically receive a minimum control-size adjustment. Your interface-size preference still applies on top.

releases.title: More battlefield. Fewer labels.
releases.summary: Compact icon controls open the actions you need, with names and costs where decisions happen.
changes: Reach Base, Economy and Army through compact icons with unit counts and economy alerts. Tap Economy or Army again to close its panel.
Move, attack, select an area and expand camera or extra orders from recognizable icons. Armed commands stay highlighted; Info and optional holds explain every action.
Recruit from unit portraits with clear names and full costs. Queue badges show pending units; Repeat keeps its ON/OFF state and any shortage visible.
See more building choices at once, with names, prices and requirements retained. Finite Farm food remains explicit.
Read food, wood, gold and population from distinct symbols and numerical counters. Larger maps, camera zoom and match rules are unchanged.

releases.title: Room to explore. Room to fight.
releases.summary: Larger battlefields, a wider camera view and more reasons to scout the flanks.
changes: Every population setting now plays on a 72 by 72 battlefield, with more than twice the previous area.
Discover two finite food, wood and gold expansion pockets on each side. Nearby opening resources remain balanced between rivals.
Zoom farther out for an overview. Wheel and button zoom ease around your focus; small trackpad movements make smaller adjustments. Pinch follows your fingers, and Reduced motion keeps zoom immediate.

Villagers work through each gathering cycle faster for both players, with wood gathering matching food to help fund buildings and reinforcements. Resources still need real delivery, Farms still run out, and every recruit and building still costs resources.
AI workers keep looking for new resources when a search route is blocked, so trapped workers cannot use up the whole team's exploration plan. The opponent still has to scout before finding resources.

Standard now needs four minutes of Sacred control. Contests pause your clock and losing ownership resets it. Control race keeps banking its four minutes across captures; destroying the enemy Town Center still wins either mode.

releases.title: Your kingdom, ready to go
releases.summary: A proper welcome in your browser. A direct route into the game from your Home Screen.
changes: Learn the game and find installation steps for iPhone, iPad, Android and desktop.
Play in your browser whenever you prefer. Installation is optional.
Online update checks happen automatically. Ready updates apply at the main menu, with active matches and their results protected.
Find these release notes from the welcome page, main menu or Pause screen.

releases.title: Keep your kingdom in the fight
releases.summary: Clearer economy decisions and a new optional way to contest the map.
changes: Economy now warns when worked food is running low and explains finite Farms: 75 wood buys a field containing 300 food.
See production shortages, counter roles and rally destinations without relying on tooltips.
Economy and Army stay open when a selected unit falls, so the next reinforcement order remains within reach.
Control race offers cheaper paid Feudal and military buildings. Bank four minutes of exclusive Sacred control; contests pause scoring. Standard rules remain available.
Report a problem directly from the result screen using the existing private report flow.

releases.title: Less menu work. More strategy.
releases.summary: Mobile management, deliberate gestures and persistent settings.
changes: Reach Base, Economy and Army quickly, save two groups, and manage paid production away from home.
Reassign workers, follow raid warnings and locate the Sacred site while keeping the battlefield visible.
Adjust interface size, camera and audio preferences. Settings stay on this device.
Web audio routing and background transitions have been improved.
